stem.en: Kabir reads that "fermentation is how microbes make energy without oxygen". What is the honest version?

text.en: Fermentation makes no energy itself. Glycolysis makes two coins. Fermentation empties the buckets so glycolysis can keep making two coins, over and over, without oxygen.

feedback.en: Count the coins in the Lens. Glycolysis: two. Fermentation: zero. The label credits the wrong step.

text.en: Fermentation makes thirty coins like the powerhouse.

feedback.en: Thirty needs the staircase and oxygen. Fermentation gets two per glucose, which is why it eats so much sugar.

text.en: Fermentation makes coins from the acid.

feedback.en: The acid is waste, dumped so the bucket can be reused. It still holds most of the glucose's fall, unused.

explanation.en: Follow the coins and the buckets separately. Coins come from glycolysis. Fermentation is the bucket-emptying step, and it is worth nothing in coins and everything in keeping the pipeline open.
